proof: For odd numbers of face pieces, the difference and sum conditions force initial angles in multiples of π/5. In the initial corner sector these four rays reach the two adjacent vertices and the two proper diagonals before any further face crossing. The diagonals give precisely the two extra bare-angle paths.

For even numbers of face pieces, the transported clockwise terminal edge direction −2π/5 determines q1=h(p0) on the double pentagon. Reflection and reversal return the same corner sector and tangent, removing any ambiguity from multiple sectors at the translation-surface singularity. The regular midpoint is fixed by h, so it lies at a glued-edge midpoint.

The physical half-turn about that edge midpoint reverses both intrinsic tangent coordinates and exchanges the two endpoint vertices. If these vertices were at distance two, the unique common neighbor in the girth-five graph would be fixed, contrary to the order-three rotational vertex stabilizer. Edge paths themselves have distance one.

The public face word is regular up to its first terminal vertex, at graph distance two. Its transported outgoing ray leads to relative angle 144 degrees; outward physical boundary gives a different ray. Separately the displayed coordinate identity evaluates to (425+189√5)/2, exceeding the valid word norm by 59+26√5.
